subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm designing a six-wheeled, three-axle carrier vehicle with a long railgun mounted on top and stabilizer legs for deployment, keeping it manageable with roughly 150 static parts and a few SVG hazard-stripe decals rather than a complex jointed rig.

I'm working out the layout: a 9m-long, 3m-wide hull with front cab, placing the wheel axles front-to-back along the chassis and picking a military color palette of olive drab, dark steel, warning yellow, and glowing cyan accents for the rail energy effects.

Now I'm sketching the cab geometry with a sloped windscreen using an extruded profile defined in the z-y plane, building out the front wedge shape point by point.

I'm adding a windscreen as a slanted dark glass plane positioned along the front slope's normal direction, plus side window planes on each flank, before moving on to the rear deck design.

Now I'm laying out the chassis geometry: a lower box forming the main body, a raised deck section behind it, and fender boxes positioned above the wheel locations to cover them from the sides.

For the wheels, I'm designing each as a cylinder with dark tire coloring plus a steel hub cylinder and a ring of six small lug nut cylinders, considering whether to add tread blocks as merged boxes around the tire for extra detail.

To keep the rig stable without joints causing orphaned parts, I'll create a root "hull" joint that everything attaches to, plus individual wheel joints for spinning and leg joints for the stabilizers.

Each wheel gets its own joint attached to the hull along the x-axis, with merged tread geometry bound to it. The stabilizer legs are hinge joints branching from the hull, extending diagonally outward and then down to foot pads touching the ground, with two legs placed front and rear on each side.

I'm working out where exactly to place the stabilizers relative to the axle positions (front, mid, rear) and the cab's z-span, trying to settle on z-coordinates that keep the legs clear of the wheels while still bracing the vehicle, with arms rising from deck height before angling out and down.

I'll settle on legs at z=1.8 and -3.7 for a wider, slightly asymmetric stance. For the railgun turret, I'm placing a rotating ring base with cheek plates holding the gun pivot elevated above the cab, working out the pivot height and angle so the barrel clears the cab roof when aimed forward.

Now I'm figuring out the barrel geometry using a direction-and-up frame helper—paired rails, breech block, capacitor banks, glowing coil rings, and muzzle brake, all positioned relative to the aim direction with lateral offsets for the twin rails.

Adding the glowing plasma strip between rails and insulator spacer blocks...

Now adding capacitor cylinders flanking the barrel with glowing bands, a flared muzzle frustum, and glowing rail strips along the inner faces. I'm also placing hydraulic elevation actuators connecting deck to gun underside, plus a rear generator module with cooling fins and exhaust pipes, and glowing capacitor racks along the deck sides.

For the cab, I'm detailing mirrors, glowing headlights, a light bar, antennas, a roof sensor pod with dish, a front bumper with winch and tow hooks, armor plating with a wedge shape, hazard stripe textures, a unit emblem decal with "R-9" markings, and red glowing taillights with exhaust stacks behind the cab. I'm planning around six textures total -- hazard stripes, emblem, glass, vent grille, a "HIGH VOLTAGE" warning plate, and cyan rail glow -- along with an olive camo paint scheme with darker mottling in a cel-shaded style.

Now I'm working out the custom paint logic using noise and mottle functions layered with countershading and a dirt gradient near the base, pulling in the glow kit for lighting effects. I'm checking that the wheels, tires, and stabilizer pads properly contact the ground plane, placing the axle mostly hidden beneath the chassis, and sizing the tire sidewalls using a cylinder geometry for the dark rubber look.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Now I'm planning the joint hierarchy: hull root, turret hinge, gun pivot child of turret, with parts assigned to their respective bones since orientation doesn't matter for a static pose. I still need to work out the stabilizer joints—arm and piston hinges—and their roles.

I'm setting up helper functions: a box builder that wraps the geometry, color, position, and bone assignment, plus a glow helper for emissive strength, and planning how paint/UV coloring applies to the box parts.

Defining color constants for the military palette and writing the procedural hull paint function that blends olive tones with noise-based camo patterning...

Now I'm placing chassis side details like toolboxes and a fuel tank cylinder, checking coordinates carefully so the tank doesn't overlap the wheels or stabiliser arms along the z-axis.

For the rear deck I'm adding a generator box and checking it against the turret and gun breech's swept position, finding a slight overlap at full elevation so I'm shrinking the generator's depth and shifting it further back to clear the breech.

I'm now defining the gun housing itself: a cylindrical base at the turret joint, side cheeks as boxes flanking the pivot, and a trunnion cylinder running through the pivot point for the barrel to rotate on.

Setting up a helper function to compute aim-direction vectors and another to place colored parts at offsets along the gun's axis, so I can build the breech housing, recoil box, and capacitor cylinders consistently along the barrel's length.

Still designing piston details...

I'm defining joint assignments for stabilizer arm and piston, then planning out hazard stripe, emblem, glass, vent, and warning textures for the model, plus headlight glow boxes at the front.

Now I'm placing the front bumper, winch cylinder, grille vent plane, and headlights with specific positions and sizes, then adding emblem planes on the cab doors.

Side window glass panes go at the cab, and I'm positioning the chassis emblem lower between the wheels and tank, checking it clears the arm height. I also need to account for plane orientation so text faces outward correctly on both sides.

Now I'm working out the windshield's sloped plane geometry: computing the outward normal from the cab's angled face, centering it between the roof and belt line, and sizing it to match the cab width with an upward lean for correct orientation.

I'm placing the roof sensor pod, amber light bar, and twin antenna rods, then adding mirror arms. For the exhaust, I'm setting vertical cylindrical stacks on either side behind the cab, capped at the top, with the rear stack tucked onto the deck just behind the cabin. Finally I'm positioning the rear tail lights with a red glow and a hazard warning plate at the back of the vehicle.

Now I'm adding the rear tow hitch, a warning label near the generator, and an antenna mounted there too. I'm laying out capacitor racks along the deck sides as small boxes with glowing slots on top, careful to keep them clear of the turret radius and cab footprint, and finishing with a set of thin cooling fin boxes and vent textures on the generator housing.

Next I'm sketching the wheel fenders as thin boxes positioned above each wheel arch, plus dark mudflaps trailing behind, while checking they sit correctly relative to the chassis width and deck overhang. Then I'm starting to tally up the total part count, beginning with the six wheel assemblies each made of tire, rim, cap, tread, and lug nuts merged together.

Still positioning lug nuts and finalizing cylinder rotations... then I'll add flat shading for the cylinder parts and write everything out with the part colors defined.

I'm adding an emissive glow helper for lit parts, setting up text elements for the emblem, and starting the build function with a root hull joint. I'm also defining helper functions for boxes, cylinders (with flat shading and direction support), and planes to streamline part creation.

Now I'm working out the gun's pivot joint and angle, then sketching the breech housing, top armor wedge, and rail details along the barrel with their positions and colors.

Still placing rail components...

Adding piston rods connecting deck to breech, then placing a sight/scope assembly on the side and a warning label plane oriented to face outward on the breech surface.

Now I'm laying out the turret: a base cylinder with a slewing ring, cheeks aligned at the correct z-offset so the turret pivot matches the deck, plus the generator housing and ammo racks positioned along the hull.

I'm checking clearances between the racks and turret ring, deciding to skip extra details like cab ladders and guardrails but adding a toolbox and spare parts for visual interest. I'm making sure the tire bottoms sit exactly at y=0 so the whole model rests on the ground plane, and considering dark non-slip deck plating.

Now I'm generating SVG hazard-stripe textures with diagonal black-and-yellow patterns for the vehicle markings.

Writing more SVG textures...

I'm finalizing the remaining textures—a circular pad, an emblem with a star and "RG-6" text, a glass gradient with glint highlights, vent slats, and a warning triangle—then adding a cyan glow strip along the gun barrel while skipping underside chassis lights.
